items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: I saw Williams and Walker before they ever hit Broadway.

ctx.x: All this business, you're talking about the thing of the nigger blues. You know, didn't you, the term nigger did not used to be derogatory at all. No. Back in the old days.

Well, in the old days, they were Negro minstrels and used it freely among themselves, back and forth. It was common with them, too, you see. That's right. That's the idea of there. The whole thing, the whole attitude was different, for instance. Now, they would get up. I saw Williams and Walker before they ever hit Broadway. And they were, Williams was the dumb Negro, and Walker was the flashy, smart Negro, kidding back and forth, you know. And, of course, if you want to take literally the gags, they passed back…

And that's what they do. They still wouldn't be doing today that's what they do. They didn't get into all this stuff. Well, they... I got to talking to Cliff about that one time. He said, oh, no, that's what they don't. He says, you can insult a man anytime you want to. You can tell. I don't care how you call it or how you pronounce it. He says, I know what you mean. Sure. And if you mean to insult me, you can call me until you want it.
